The reminder fired because the parser misread the message text as flags. I fixed it and committed the fix as `98187d2`.

**Cause:** `src/staging.py` checks each short-option word for the stage-all letter (`a` for `commit`). `git commit -m"add export handler"` reaches the parser as one word, `-madd export handler`. The check scanned the whole word, so the `a` inside "add" in the message matched as `-a`.

**Fix:** The scan now stops at an option that takes a value (`m`, `F`, `C`, `c`, `t`, `S` for commit). Whatever follows such an option in the same word is its value, not flags. So `-am` still counts as stage-all, and `-madd` and `-ma` don't.

**Tests:** I added `git commit -m"add export handler"`, `git commit -madd` and `git commit -ma 'fix'` to the "passes" cases in `tests/test_staging.py`. The suite passes (2 tests, `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest tests.test_staging`), and the reported command now returns `False`. I didn't run the new cases against the old code; by reading it, the old check returns `True` for the first one, so the test would have failed before the fix.

The commit touches only `src/staging.py` and `tests/test_staging.py`. Your pending `README.md` change and the untracked `notes/` directory are untouched. The commit message ends with the Haiku co-author line you specified.
